sections.html:
Wood County sits in the Toledo area, with the courthouse in Bowling Green. Population is 134,176 in 54,257 households, and owners hold 64.4 percent of the homes. The middle home value is $227,600. Fifteen school districts draw on county land, and about 80 taxing districts set separate rates, so two houses a few miles apart can carry quite different bills.

The Auditor sets values and the Treasurer sends and collects bills. Call the Auditor about the value and the Treasurer about what you owe. Both offices are at the Bowling Green courthouse square.

sections.h2: What the 2026 triennial update did to home values
sections.html:
Residential values rose 19 percent on average countywide. The state runs a full reappraisal every sixth year with an update in between. The county did its reappraisal in 2023, which made 2026 the mid-cycle adjustment.

The new values apply to tax year 2026, which is collected in February and July 2027, with a January 1, 2026 lien date. Only arm's length sales from the prior three years feed the statistics. A single parcel can land above or below the average depending on location and condition.

Your bill will not track the new value dollar for dollar. Three state laws soften the jump. House Bill 920 reduces voted outside millage when values climb, House Bill 186 gives school districts an inflation cap credit, and House Bill 335 gives the same credit on inside millage, the unvoted portion held to 10 mills. A plain renewal levy holds its millage, a renewal with an increase raises it, and an additional levy adds a new tax.

sections.h2: Due dates, penalties and how to pay
sections.html:
Real estate and manufactured home taxes come due in February and July, on dates the Treasurer announces each year. A late payment adds 5 percent in the first 10 days and 10 percent after that.

Ways to pay the Wood County Treasurer
Payment methodHow it works
OnlineTax Search on the Treasurer's site, by card or e-check; the office does not collect a convenience fee
PhoneAutomated line, 419-359-0006
Drop boxSummit Street entrance of the courthouse
MailWood County Treasurer, One Courthouse Square, Bowling Green, OH 43402
Participating banksBranches in Bowling Green, Perrysburg, Grand Rapids, Custar, Deshler, North Baltimore, Fostoria, Pemberville and Gibsonburg
Auto payFree bank withdrawal; the form comes from the Treasurer

A postmark decides whether a mailed payment is on time, and sorting machines may stamp a later day than the day you posted it. Mail it early, or hand it to the counter clerk for a hand stamp. Call 419-354-9130 with questions.

A formal complaint goes to the Auditor for the Board of Revision. The filing window runs January 1 through March 31, and for the 2026 values the last day is March 31, 2027. An informal review with the Auditor is a common first step.

  • For an informal review, bring a recent appraisal (under two years old), three or more comparable sales from 2023 to 2025, or a sales listing.
  • A disputed amount above $50,000 requires a Board of Revision filing.
  • The Sales List, Sales Search and Comp Search tools pull comparable sales, and Comp Search is the most useful of the three.
  • R.C. 5715.19 lets an owner file only one complaint in each interim period. A sale, casualty loss, major improvement or change in occupancy after the lien date opens an exception.

The real estate office, on the county office building's second floor, answers at 419-354-9173.

The Auditor offers these programs to lower the tax on a home or farm.

  • Homestead exemption, for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled. The income ceiling is $40,000 for late applicants on tax year 2025 and $41,000 for new applicants on tax year 2026, and the house must be the primary residence.
  • Disabled veteran homestead exemption, for a qualifying veteran or a surviving spouse.
  • Owner occupied reduction, by application, for the home an owner lives in.
  • Agricultural use valuation, for 10 or more acres in farming, with a $25.00 fee on new applications and a penalty if the land is sold, drops under 10 acres or stops being farmed.

These programs come by application through the Auditor, so nothing is applied automatically. Bring proof of age or disability, proof the house is your primary residence, and income records where an income ceiling applies. A buyer does not inherit your exemption, and the reduction usually ends when the deed changes hands, so expect the next bill to look different.

A free agricultural district application protects farmland from certain water and sewer assessments. Homestead questions go to 419-354-9167, and agricultural programs to 419-354-9174.

sections.h2: What a seller pays when the deed transfers
sections.html:
The Wood County Auditor charges $3.00 per $1,000 of price on a deed, with the price rounded up to the nearest hundred, and adds $0.50 per parcel as a transfer fee. A deed that qualifies as exempt goes on form DTE 100(EX).

R.C. 319.202 has the buyer file a value statement and puts the fee on the seller. The form also asks about farm valuation and any recoupment charge.

The Auditor's real estate page links to Sheriff Sales and a file of pending special assessments for 2026.

The tax lien stays with the parcel, so any balance is settled at or before closing. Before you sign a purchase contract, do these three things.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the current balance, including any unpaid February or July installment.
  • Ask the Auditor about pending special assessments on the parcel.
  • Ask the title company how the balance will be paid out of your proceeds.

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender's appraisal or underwriting, but the tax balance still gets paid from the sale. Knowing the number early keeps it from surprising anyone at the table.

A closing that falls between the two installments usually splits the bill between seller and buyer under the contract's proration terms. Ask the title company how it figures that split on your closing statement.

The Treasurer collects two kinds of property tax, real estate under R.C. 323.12 and manufactured homes under R.C. 4503.06, and both come due in February and July. A manufactured home is billed at the combined rate of the district where it sits, and a 1998 law moved its valuation toward market value, as with real estate.

  • Conveyance fee on a mobile home: $1.00 per $1,000 of price, rounded up to the nearest thousand, plus $0.50 per title. No money changing hands means no fee.
  • Mobile home moving permit: $5.00, with a $100.00 fine for moving one without a permit.
  • Wood County's sales tax rate is 6.75 percent.

faqs.q: Which months do Wood County property taxes fall due?
faqs.a: They fall due in February and July, on dates the Treasurer sets. Late payments cost 5 percent in the first 10 days and 10 percent afterward.

faqs.q: By how much did Wood County residential values change in 2026?
faqs.a: They rose 19 percent on average. Neighborhoods differ, and House Bills 920, 186 and 335 keep bills from rising as fast as values.

faqs.q: What is the last day for a Wood County Board of Revision complaint?
faqs.a: March 31 each year, which is March 31, 2027 for tax year 2026. The window opens January 1.

faqs.q: What does a Wood County deed cost at the Auditor?
faqs.a: The fee is $3.00 per $1,000 of price, rounded up to the nearest hundred, plus $0.50 per parcel.

faqs.q: Which Wood County office answers tax questions?
faqs.a: Payments and bills go to the Treasurer at 419-354-9130. Value questions go to the Auditor's real estate office at 419-354-9173. A toll free line, 866-860-4140, serves both.
